LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS 11.1.1 PROPER ARTICULATION OF SIGNS AND VOCABULARY: LISTENING FLUENCY OR VISUAL FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: SPORTS: MY FAVOURITE GAME Suggested vocabulary to be signed: win, lose, football
Topic 11.1: Observing and articulating signs 11.1.1 Proper articulation of signs and Vocabulary: Listening Fluency or visual fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and articulating signs 11.1.1 Proper articulation of signs and Vocabulary: Listening Fluency or visual fluency, part of SPORTS: MY FAVOURITE GAME Suggested vocabulary to be signed: win, lose, football in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: How do facial expressions and gestures help us to communicate well? 2. Why should we listen actively to what others are saying?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and articulating signs 11.1.1 Proper articulation of signs and Vocabulary: Listening Fluency or visual fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: learner develops skill of communication and self-expression as they make a three-minute signed speech.

● Self-efficacy: learner develops the skill of knowing who I am, as they role play and use non-verbal cues.

Values:
Unity: determination as learner makes short speeches using vocabulary related to the theme.

Link to other subjects

Learner is able to link the concept of sports: My favourite game to their learning in Creative arts and sports
